author_id.description: Author id, the last segment of an author key: `OL79034A` for `/authors/OL79034A`.

response.title: Author
response.description: One author record. As with a work, most fields are optional: a record grows one edit at a time.

key.description: The author's own key, such as `/authors/OL79034A`.

personal_name.description: Name in catalogue order, surname first.

alternate_names.description: Other names this author has been catalogued under.

title.description: An honorific or a role, such as `novelist`. Not a book title.

bio.description: Biography. A plain string on some records and a `TextValue` on others, exactly like a work's `description`.

links.description: External links editors attached to the author.

remote_ids.description: This author's ids in other catalogues, keyed by the catalogue's name: `wikidata`, `viaf`, `isni` and others as editors add them.

source_records.description: Where the record's data came from, one entry per import.

items.description: One source record identifier, such as `marc:harvard_bibliographic_metadata/...`.

revision.description: Revision number of the record as served.

latest_revision.description: Highest revision number the record has.

notes: `remote_ids` is a map, not a record: the catalogues an author is linked to are open-ended, so there is no fixed set of properties to name.

`birth_date` and `death_date` are served and are not declared, for the same reason a work's `first_publish_date` is not: their values are free-form human text (`8 October 1920`), so there is no wire format to declare and no conversion to promise.
